prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: WUI decision support; time sync, health checks, audit of assignment/staging changes; command continuity over automation when degraded. Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): primary UI; triage; Airspace Restricted State (helitack sees boundary, confirms); produces Crew Staging Pin; promotes fire location for aviation review; records assignment packages; flags assignments on Confirmed Ignition State change. Disconnected mode: last sync shown, cached review, queued updates, no irreversible releases; conflicts held for Redtail. Access: named accounts, RBAC, MFA, least privilege; offline: expiring signed credentials, later supervisor review; admin changes separately approved, never via field accounts. Append-only audit store; field components buffer/forward signed records unmodified. North Lookout Camera Mast: Thermal Spot Snippet, smoke bearing. South Lookout Camera Mast: bearing track, Camera Cleaning Log to Smoke Classifier Module. Masts send health telemetry. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): Battery Swap Ticket, readiness; never authorizes crew movement. Drone Tasking Service: missions pending/active/complete; not flight-release authority; degraded comms: validates Drone Corridor Permit. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): advisory scores/perimeter/hazards; applies Ridge Shadow Mask; keeps last approved model; rejects unsigned/unversioned packages. Smoke Classifier Module: Ridge Shadow Mask; never sole basis for aircraft commitment. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): Wind Shift Bulletin, exposure flags. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger): fallback relay; queues acks ≥15 min. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold): blocks incomplete releases; Runway Release Note; Suppression Drop Receipt. East Retardant Loading Pump: Retardant Batch Slip to Tanker Base Manager; metered recirculation mode. West Retardant Loading Pump: shift-change inspection. Crewline Mobile Tablet: assignments, cached staging, encrypted queue. Actors: County Emergency Liaison, Duty Detection Officer (Orion), Air Attack Supervisor, Drone Pilot Operator, Tanker Base Manager, Helitack Crew Leader (uses Crew Staging Pin in drills). Data: operational records retained per agency policy, raw sensor shorter; encryption at rest, controlled export, authorized deletion. Multi-period incidents: staged spares so no single fault stops operations. Role-based training each season and on procedure/config change; human confirmation in every decision.

New part:
S211: All operational users shall receive communications training that includes VHF Radio Gateway Repeater failure modes, alternate contact paths, call signs, message brevity, and confirmation readbacks.
S212: Weather training shall explain how the MesoWest Weather Fusion Node supports situational awareness and how operators should treat weather inputs when local observations conflict with displayed values.
S213: Initial qualification shall include supervised console practice, scenario walkthroughs, and a documented check by an instructor who is authorized by the operations lead.
S214: Annual refresher training shall include changes to software screens, revised thresholds, updated contact rosters, seasonal hazard briefings, and lessons learned from prior incidents.
S215: Tabletop exercises shall be conducted before the expected peak fire period and shall test detection triage, command notification, airspace coordination, tanker-base coordination, crew deployment, and public-agency liaison actions.
S216: Live exercises shall be scheduled at least once per season when conditions permit and shall include field crews, aircraft coordination staff, drone operations staff, and command-center personnel.
S217: Exercise controllers shall inject realistic complications such as intermittent network service, obscured camera views, delayed field confirmation, resource conflicts, and conflicting reports from external observers.
S218: Performance measures shall include time from automated detection to human review, time from review to command notification, time to resource assignment, communication completion rate, and accuracy of incident status updates.
S219: Detection quality shall be evaluated using confirmed events, benign smoke sources, weather-related artifacts, and operator notes so that both missed detections and false alarms are visible to program management.
S220: Every false-alarm review shall identify the apparent cause, affected sensors or analytic outputs, operator actions, dispatch consequences, and any recommended tuning or training change.
S221: The review board shall include operations, aviation, field crew, maintenance, and county liaison representatives when the event affected more than one operational function.
S222: Seasonal readiness shall require each active user to demonstrate current proficiency, complete required safety briefings, and acknowledge the current operating procedures before receiving operational access.
S223: Personnel who do not meet proficiency requirements shall complete remedial training and a repeat evaluation before performing unsupervised duties in the Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System.
S224: Deployment governance for the Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System shall be managed as a staged release process that follows completion of seasonal readiness activities.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
